marta (customer-support): Hey team - customer 'BrightAd' on dedicated pool dp-eu2 reports tail latency spikes + intermittent 429s since ~23:00 UTC. They also see unexpected billing increments when retries happen. Can we triage?

ben (eng-runtime): Seen similar across one node earlier today. Suspect noisy-neighbor on shared host (MIG slices). Any quick repro steps from the customer?

marta (customer-support): Customer says pattern: normal then sudden ~300-800ms per-token latency for ~3-7 minutes, repeated every ~30-40 minutes. They captured app logs + a quick nvidia snapshot. Sending sanitized logs below.

rohan (support): Paste from customer nvidia-smi during incident:
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-16T23:12:45Z
GPU 0 MIG 1g.5gb utilization: 97% 
GPU 1 MIG 1g.5gb utilization: 12% 
Processes: 
/usr/bin/llm_server (pid 8423) - GPU0 - 35% 
/other_heavy_job (pid 9120) - GPU0 - 60%
SM%: GPU0 94%, GPU1 14%
Memory: GPU0 4.6GB/5GB, GPU1 1.2GB/5GB
```

lina (dedicated-platform): That looks like one MIG slice hitting SM saturation while other slices idle. Could be non-Redwood workload pinned to same host (we sometimes allow colocated partner jobs for burst). Need host ID and slice ids.

marta (customer-support): Host id is host-eu2-07, MIG slices: 0 and 1. Customer included their request IDs: req=cbf1a8.., cbf1a9.. - they show a bunch of retries after 429s.

ben (eng-runtime): Two things to consider: 1) autoscaler may be reacting late (scale-up threshold set to 80% sustained); 2) our rate limiter may be returning 429s while backend is overloaded, leading client retries that amplify load and accidental billing increments because requests are accepted then retried.

sre-oncall: I can isolate node host-eu2-07 briefly. Suggest drain the slice and shift customer to another slice to confirm noisy neighbor. If mitigation succeeds, we'll set a temp autoscale bump.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler alert: dp-eu2 utilization spike at 2026-03-16T23:11Z -> scaled from 4->5 instances at 23:28Z (delay 17m). Policy: scale_on_p95_cpu > 70% for 5m.

marta (customer-support): Customer also flagged billing anomalies: multiple charge events around the spike window. Kevin (billing) looping in.

kevin (billing): We see repeated short-lived accepted requests with retry flags in logs; our billing pipeline currently counts accepted token units even when client retries. We'll need to dedupe by request_id if they supply it. Can we get them to send request-id header?

ben (eng-runtime): For repro: if we can force a small load on MIG slice 0 to saturate SM and then run the customer's request pattern on slice 1, we can observe cross-slice interference and tail latency bump. I'll prepare a small repro script.

rohan (support): Customer willing to run repro in their staging. They can run: 
```bash
# aggressive GPU micro-benchmark to saturate SM units
python sm_stress.py --gpu 0 --duration 300 --load 0.9
# then run their request flood at p50 RPS
wrk -t4 -c50 https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '@payload.json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Request-ID: test-repro-001'
```

lina (dedicated-platform): In parallel, I'll pull node metrics and MIG allocation: 
`kubectl get nodes host-eu2-07 -o json | jq .status.allocatable`
And audit our placement logs: which tenant got collocated partner jobs. If collocated job is non-Redwood we can evict.

ben (eng-runtime): If repro shows SM saturation causing tail spikes, mitigation options: - pin critical tenant to isolated MIG (flip placement policy) - temporarily increase autoscale aggressiveness (lower thresholds to 50%, reduce cool-down) - rate-limiter soft-queue requests to smooth bursts

marta (customer-support): Customer asks for ETA to fix — they said this impacts live campaigns. Any temporary workaround?

sre-oncall: Immediate: move BrightAd off host-eu2-07 to a different host in dp-eu2 (rolling move). Will do a targeted migrate now, expect <5m interruption.

autoscale-bot: Migration initiated for tenant BrightAd -> host-eu2-11 at 2026-03-16T23:41:12Z.

marta (customer-support): Customer reports latency returning to normal after migration (~10m). They still want root cause so it doesn't recur.

ben (eng-runtime): Agreed. Next steps: 1) collect pprof traces for their requests during spike window; 2) gather GPU perf counters (SM occupancy, L2 cache evictions) from host; 3) confirm if collocated job was an allowed partner or rogue workload.

lina (dedicated-platform): I'll open an internal incident to track: INC-2026-042, assign to eng-runtime + infra. Also proposing policy change: default: single-tenant MIG for Dedicated Premium customers to avoid noisy neighbor.

kevin (billing): For billing, we'll implement request_id dedupe to avoid double-charges on retry loops. Short-term: bill credit for affected window for BrightAd.

marta (customer-support): Thanks everyone. I'll update customer with mitigation, credit, and an ETA for RCA.

ben (eng-runtime): I'll post repro artifacts and perf counters to the incident channel when collected.

ops-bot: Ticket INC-2026-042 created and linked to thread.

marta (customer-support): Closing loop: customer accepted credit and will run repro in staging tomorrow. They'll provide X-Request-ID headers for dedupe testing. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:
